why: A declared vantage aimed at something the server never sends. The site plan's `view/the-approach` stands its eye at (32, 88, 60) and looks at the hall; this edit moves what it looks at 360 blocks down the z axis. The gallery declares `world.view_distance: 12`, which serves 192 blocks in every direction, so the thing this view is of is never sent to a client standing at its eye and the picture the walk would judge cannot render. The refusal names the fewest chunks that would serve it (23) — one edit to the one field — and the same rule meets a `sightlines[]` entry longer than the radius, a showcase camera whose subject is past it, and a cutscene keyframe farther from its aim than it.
